item.title: Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand: lenders pause billions in data centre and GPU loans tied to ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent after US chip curbs
item.description: Bloomberg reported on 26 November, via The Straits Times, that lenders have slowed or dropped data centre and GPU loans linked to Chinese tenants after the BIS rule that took effect on 19 November. Some lenders are doing more due diligence on an upsized $6.6 billion loan sought by Bain Capital's Bridge Data Centres, whose Malaysian facilities serve ByteDance. One bank passed on a fully underwritten $372 million loan for Partners Group-backed Digital Halo (Malaysia, serving Alibaba). Banks are reassessing a $480 million loan for Singapore neocloud Aolani, and at least one fund dropped out of a $300 million GMI Cloud loan for a Thai data centre to be used by Tencent. DayOne has put its US listing plans on hold, and UOB's roughly $1 billion risk transfer has slowed. Fitch said on 26 November that Asia-Pacific data centre investment will slow and become more selective, with neoclouds under the most pressure. Caveat: deal details rest on anonymous sources; the companies declined to comment or did not respond. Country conversion: export-licence risk is now converting directly into a financing freeze for Southeast Asian AI capacity that serves Chinese tenants. [Signal 50, Single-source, via Bloomberg via The Straits Times, 26 Nov 2026; Fitch Ratings via Reuters, 26 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Southeast Asia: Nvidia tells server partners to stop shipping to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia
item.description: The Financial Times reported on 26 November that Nvidia has instructed its manufacturing partners to halt server deliveries to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, and that partners including Dell and Supermicro have told customers in those countries that Nvidia will not authorise their shipments. It is unclear whether the halt is temporary while Nvidia and partners work out compliance with the BIS interim final rule, effective 19 November, which requires licences for advanced chips to those countries and Brazil and for overseas data centres serving China-headquartered customers above a threshold of roughly 750 H100s. The FT noted Nvidia booked $104 billion of 2025 revenue through its Singapore subsidiary. Separately, CNBC reported on 25 November that sellers have floated deals for thousands of B300 GPUs since the rule was announced; no prices or completed sales were reported. Caveat: Nvidia did not comment; this goes further than the 20 November Nikkei report of individual partners pausing. Country conversion: Southeast Asia's pipeline of Nvidia capacity is frozen at the vendor level, not only by individual OEMs. [Signal 48, Single-source, via Financial Times via Reuters, 26 Nov 2026; TrendForce; CNBC, 25 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: China: Z.AI's GLM-5.5 slips and Moonshot sees release cycles doubling as overseas compute access is curbed
item.description: Reuters reported exclusively on 26 November that Z.AI (Zhipu) had planned to release its roughly 3 trillion parameter GLM-5.5 in November but has not, held up partly by anti-distillation safeguards, and that the new US computing restrictions could push the launch into the first quarter of 2027 or later. Moonshot AI, which rents compute and prioritises overseas providers, internally expects its six-month interval between major releases could stretch to 12 months or longer if overseas access is cut off, with Kimi K4 possibly delayed to around mid-2027; a source said domestic capacity could not make up the shortfall. Moonshot is stepping up efforts to rent compute in Europe and plans to approach Chinese chipmakers. Caveat: anonymous sources; neither company commented. Country conversion: the BIS remote-access rule is translating into measurable delays for Chinese frontier model output that relied on offshore Nvidia capacity. [Signal 40, Single-source, via Reuters exclusive, 26 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: South Korea: KT Cloud signs as master tenant for Keppel's 60 MW Ansan AI data centre
item.description: Keppel said on 26 November that Keppel Data Centre Fund III has secured kt cloud as master tenant for the full capacity of its 60 MW greenfield data centre in Ansan, in the Seoul metropolitan area, with construction starting this month and service targeted for 2030. The eight-storey facility will have liquid cooling for high-density AI. KT Cloud broke ground on a separate 50 MW Ansan facility in October and plans to run them as an integrated campus; it targets up to 1 GW of AI capacity by 2031. Caveat: lease value and rent were not disclosed by Keppel; a Korean filing values KT Cloud's right-of-use asset at about KRW 653.5 billion. Country conversion: Korean AI demand is converting into fully pre-let capacity near Seoul, but with a 2030 delivery date. [Signal 30, Confirmed, via Keppel press release, 26 Nov 2026; DCD] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Australia: Sharon AI installs 8,208 Nvidia B300s in Sydney for India's ESDS, billing from January 2027
item.description: A regulatory filing by Indian cloud provider ESDS Software Solution, reported by w.media and DCD on 26 November, says Sharon AI has installed a cluster of 8,208 Nvidia B300 GPUs for ESDS in Sydney, now in final testing, with handover expected in mid-December and billing from January 2027. The five-year contract signed in April 2026 was valued by Sharon AI at $1.25 billion. Revenue had earlier been expected from the third quarter of 2026; the parties agreed to defer acceptance until testing is complete. Caveat: delivery slipped about two quarters. Country conversion: Australia is converting into an offshore B300 host for an Indian cloud, outside the five licence-required countries. [Signal 28, Confirmed, via ESDS regulatory filing via w.media and DCD, 26 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Portugal: Fortitude Capital plans 202 MW Hermes AI campus in Sines
item.description: Portuguese investment firm Fortitude Capital is developing the Hermes Data Center, a 202 MW greenfield campus for AI and HPC workloads in the Sines Industrial and Logistics Zone, DCD reported on 26 November. Hermes was added to the portfolio of zone manager Aicep Global Parques after Iberdrola withdrew its Green Ammonia Express project, which had reserved 21 hectares. Sines already hosts Start Campus, planned for up to 1.2 GW of IT. Caveat: no investment figure, power contract, tenant or timeline was disclosed. Country conversion: Sines is converting land freed from a cancelled green hydrogen project into a second AI campus. [Signal 22, Single-source, via DCD (from DCD Spanish/Portuguese edition), 26 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: S&P puts Nvidia's AA rating on CreditWatch Negative as AI borrowers' default swaps hit records
item.description: S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's AA issuer and senior unsecured ratings on CreditWatch with negative implications on 25 November, citing management and governance deficiencies exposed by the CEO's resignation and reinstatement and questions over export control compliance; any cut within 90 days would likely be one notch to AA-. Nvidia priced $25 billion of senior notes in June and backs some partners' debt, leases and hardware purchases. Reuters reported on 25 November that five-year CDS spreads for Oracle, Alphabet, SpaceX and CoreWeave hit record levels overnight per S&P Global Market Intelligence, with SoftBank at 501 basis points, its widest since October 2022; Investing.com put Oracle's five-year CDS at a record 356 basis points. Nvidia closed down 3.9 per cent at $149.30 on 25 November. Caveat: CDS levels are third-party marks; S&P said Nvidia's business position is unchanged for now. Country conversion: the cost of capital behind US AI capacity is rising at the top of the stack, including for the vendor that guarantees neocloud commitments. [Signal 44, Corroborated, via S&P Global Ratings via CNBC and Reuters, 25 Nov 2026; Reuters, 25 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Air Force seeks commercial models for a 30,000-GPU, roughly $2 billion aerospace AI supercomputer
item.description: The Air Force District of Washington posted a sources-sought notice, DAF Advanced Aerospace Computing, on SAM.gov around 25 November for a purpose-built aerospace HPC and AI supercomputer of up to about 30,000 GPUs or equivalent, for tensor workloads, physical AI, large model training and dense simulation. It estimates about $2 billion of computing equipment and data centre facilities and asks about public-private models, take-or-pay or anchor-tenant commitments for non-defense capacity, and pricing tiers for dedicated GPU capacity with public-interest preemption clauses. The current site has about 750 kW of room power, scalable to 30 MW with substation capacity, plus a planned further 30 MW pad and batteries. Responses are due 11 December. Caveat: a market survey, not a procurement or award. Country conversion: the US military is moving to own frontier-class compute through financed public-private structures, adding sovereign demand to the US build. [Signal 34, Confirmed, via SAM.gov notice FA7014 via DCD, 26 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: China: GDS cuts 2026 capex guidance by 20 per cent to about $1.2 billion
item.description: GDS Holdings reported third-quarter 2026 net revenue of about $477 million, up 10 per cent year on year, with adjusted EBITDA up 2.8 per cent to $207 million (43.4 per cent margin) and utilisation of 81.2 per cent, up 6.8 points. Area committed and pre-committed rose 25.5 per cent to 823,876 square metres. GDS cut its full-year capex expectation to about $1.2 billion from the $1.5 billion guided last quarter, citing its preliminary view of the business situation and market conditions; revenue guidance was unchanged. Caveat: GDS did not tie the cut to any specific customer or to export controls. Country conversion: China's largest independent operator is filling existing halls but pulling back new spend, consistent with constrained access to accelerators. [Signal 30, Confirmed, via GDS Holdings Q3 2026 results via DCD, 25 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Ohio Power Siting Board approves 800 MW behind-the-meter gas plant for EdgeConneX despite local referendum
item.description: The Ohio Power Siting Board approved an up to 800 MW natural gas plant to power an EdgeConneX data centre behind the meter in Ashville, Pickaway County, the Ohio Capital Journal reported and DCD relayed on 25 November. About 81 per cent of Ashville voters had rejected the village's agreement with EdgeConneX in a midterm referendum; the board said it holds final permitting authority and found the project in the public interest, citing economic benefits, council support and construction noise limits. EdgeConneX had offered up to $102 million to the community. Opponents have 30 days to seek rehearing, then a possible Ohio Supreme Court appeal. Caveat: a separate 430 MW EdgeConneX gas plant for New Albany is still in filing. Country conversion: state regulators are overriding local votes to convert gas into on-site data centre power. [Signal 26, Corroborated, via Ohio Capital Journal; DCD, 25 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: South Korea: Samsung faces an HBM base die crunch as internal demand is seen doubling to 30,000 wafers a month
item.description: TrendForce reported on 25 November, citing industry sources, that Samsung's memory division will need roughly 30,000 4nm-equivalent base die wafers a month in 2027, about double this year, and that 4nm base die output is confined to select foundry lines at Hwaseong and Pyeongtaek. Samsung reportedly plans to convert its Giheung R&D line to 4nm base die, dedicate part of Pyeongtaek P5 to base die, and tentatively earmark Taylor P2 in Texas for HBM5 base dies for AMD and Nvidia; it is also said to be developing an HBM4E custom base die for Meta on its 2nm process. Hankyung reports Samsung targets doubling HBM4/HBM4E output in 2027, with HBM wafer input rising from 180,000 to 250,000 a month. Caveat: unconfirmed by Samsung. Country conversion: custom HBM is pulling Korean foundry capacity, and part of it to Texas, into the AI memory chain. [Signal 36, Single-source, via TrendForce, 25 Nov 2026, citing Seoul Economic Daily, Maeil Business, The Bell, Hankyung] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Dell books $60.2 billion of AI server orders and ends Q3 with a record $132.3 billion AI backlog
item.description: Dell Technologies reported fiscal 2027 third-quarter results on 24 November: revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103 per cent year on year, with AI-optimized server revenue of $22.0 billion, up 291 per cent, and Infrastructure Solutions Group revenue of $42.0 billion. Dell booked $60.2 billion of AI orders in the quarter and ended with a record $132.3 billion AI backlog, which COO Jeff Clarke said was vetted for customer quality and access to capital, land and power. Full-year guidance rose to $202.0 billion of revenue (from $192.0 billion) and $78.0 billion of AI-optimized server revenue (from $74.0 billion). Caveat: backlog is not revenue, and Dell shares fell with chip stocks on 25 November as AI spending and financing concerns resurfaced. Country conversion: US AI factory demand is still converting into firm server orders at OEM level, even as OEMs reprice contracts for memory inflation. [Signal 50, Confirmed, via Dell Technologies Q3 FY27 press release, 24 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Finland: XTX Markets opens its first 22.5 MW Kajaani data centre and warns grid expropriation delays threaten more investment
item.description: XTX Markets said on 24 November that the first data centre on its 193-hectare Kajaani campus is open, with 22.5 MW of IT capacity and 15,000 square metres of floor space; the second facility is due in 2027. The firm has invested over EUR 400 million, mostly with Finnish contractors, and says it has ambitions to invest billions more. Power and grid connections are secured for the first two facilities, but COO Mike Irwin said expropriation permits for grid development that once took months now take years, leaving power for the third facility (due mid-2028) and later annual builds uncertain. Caveat: this is the company's own account of the permitting dispute; no government response was published. Country conversion: Finland is converting private AI compute into domestic capacity, but grid-line permitting is now the gating item. [Signal 38, Confirmed, via XTX Markets press release, 24 Nov 2026; DCD; Yle] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Estonia: Elering says data centre connection requests reach 3.3 GW, nearly twice national peak demand
item.description: Estonian transmission operator Elering told ERR on 24 November that data centre connection requests have reached 3,300 MW, nearly twice Estonia's peak electricity demand. It has signed connection agreements for 600 MW and has active offers for a further 1,300 MW, and board member Reigo Kebja said Elering is close to the point where it cannot issue new connection offers. Economy Minister Erkki Keldo said he will discuss with developers whether projects should bring new domestic generation or pay additional taxes; Finland is already considering a generation requirement. Only one major site operates today (Greenergy, Hüüru, drawing about 2 MW, planned to 200 MW by early 2028, hosting a Nebius AI factory). Caveat: many applications may never be built. Country conversion: Baltic grid headroom, not demand, is now the limit on AI load in Estonia. [Signal 36, Single-source, via ERR News, 24 Nov 2026 (Elering)] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: France: Google unit filed a 1.2 GW grid connection request for a second Indre data centre site
item.description: Mediapart reported on 23 November that Google subsidiary Tricolore Computing filed a connection request for a 1.2 GW data centre at Villedieu-sur-Indre, near Châteauroux, and that RTE proposed a connection project of about EUR 67 million that could take seven to eight years. The site was sought as a mirror of Google's confirmed Ozans project (195 acres, up to 500 MW, under CNDP public consultation; Engie signed an energy MoU this month). Google told DCD that no final decision has been made on Ozans or any other site and that these are exploratory long-term planning, not active parallel projects; the local mayor said the plan was on hold and the landowner has opposed a sale. Country conversion: hyperscaler demand in France is now reserving multi-GW grid capacity years ahead of any build decision. [Signal 34, Corroborated, via Mediapart, 23 Nov 2026; DCD; France 3 Centre-Val de Loire] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand: BIS adds seven Megaspeed-linked firms to the Entity List
item.description: The Bureau of Industry and Security filed a final rule for public inspection on 23 November (FR Doc 2026-23999, publication 25 November) adding seven entities to the Entity List for significant risk of diverting advanced computing commodities: Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd., Swiftdata Pte. Ltd. and Apex Enterprise Solutions (Singapore) in Singapore; Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd, MSFusion Sdn. Bhd. and PT Megaspeed International under Malaysia; and Megaspeed (Thailand) Co., Ltd. A licence is required for all items subject to the EAR, reviewed under a presumption of denial; goods already en route may proceed if delivered within 30 days. Malaysia's MITI said on 24 November that MIDA will tell all data centre operators not to host, lease space to or serve the listed entities. Caveat: the rule gives no detail of the alleged diversion; Megaspeed has previously denied wrongdoing. Country conversion: the first named enforcement under the new remote-access regime lands on Southeast Asian neocloud capacity, a day after Nvidia reinstated Huang. [Signal 54, Confirmed, via BIS final rule, Federal Register public inspection, 23 Nov 2026; Malaysia MITI, 24 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: TSMC files for a proposed 2nm fab in Brazos County, Texas

The filing projects almost $23 billion of capital investment and 2,099 direct jobs over 40 years, with construction from 2027 and operations by 2029. Caveat: the application says no final site decision has been made, county records show TSMC has not bought the land, and officials say Sherman is still under review. Country conversion: leading-edge logic capacity keeps moving onshore in Texas, beside the US's other planned AI fab. [Signal 42, Corroborated, via DCD, 23 Nov 2026; KBTX] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Nvidia board unanimously reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, citing input from senior US government officials
item.description: Nvidia announced on 23 November that its board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director, effective immediately, eleven days after he resigned on 12 November. The board said it received input from senior levels of the US government and, on that basis, is confident the reinstatement poses no national security risk. Harvey Jones stays as chair; Colette Kress returns to CFO only. The independent-director investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort continues, a new National Security and Export Control Committee is retaining counsel, and Nvidia is searching for a Chief Compliance Officer. Caveat: AP reports the board had rejected Huang's offer to return days earlier. Country conversion: Washington now has a visible hand in the governance of the dominant accelerator vendor, ahead of Huang's 1 December House interviews. [Signal 50, Confirmed, via Nvidia newsroom, 23 Nov 2026; AP; The Verge, 23 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Applied Digital signs a 150 MW, 18-year lease with an investment-grade hyperscaler at higher pricing

The company says the lease carries higher pricing than its prior leases. Contracted base-term revenue now exceeds $41 billion, portfolio is over 1.6 GW contracted critical IT and 2.2 GW grid-connected peak load, and about 75% of base-term revenue is investment-grade. Financing runs through its $5 billion Macquarie equity programme then project finance; delivery is expected to begin in the first half of 2028. Caveat: site and tenant not named. Country conversion: US wholesale AI capacity is still clearing at rising rates on 18-year terms despite the midterm backlash. [Signal 42, Confirmed, via Applied Digital press release, 23 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Greece: environmental filing details AWS and PPC's 300 MW Kozani campus on a retired coal plant site
item.description: An environmental impact assessment reported by OT.gr and DCD on 23 November describes the AWS campus at PPC's former Agios Dimitrios coal plant in Kozani: 300 MW power (240 MW IT) across four buildings and 20 data halls, reusing the plant's 400 kV substations through two new underground cables, with scope to reach 1 GW. PPC invests about EUR 1 billion and AWS a similar amount for IT; AWS holds exclusivity on the 1 GW option until May 2027. The 300 MW agreement is expected to be finalised by Q1 2027, construction to start summer 2027 and finish end 2028; annual water use is estimated at about 203,000 cubic metres. Caveat: based on the filing as reported, not an AWS announcement. Country conversion: Greece turns retired lignite grid capacity into a hyperscale anchor; AWS has no Greek region yet. [Signal 38, Single-source, via DCD, 23 Nov 2026, citing OT.gr and the EIA] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Indonesia: Firmus seeks a $1.5 billion bond to buy GB300s for its DayOne project, Bloomberg reports

item.title: Spain: data centre decree in force, with 80 per cent hourly-matched new renewables and curtailment duties
item.description: Royal Decree 1032/2026, approved by the Council of Ministers on 20 November and published in the BOE on 21 November, took effect on 22 November. It applies to data centres that have sought or will seek grid access and connection permits. They must cover 80 per cent of consumption with new renewable supply through self-consumption or PPAs, matched hourly, with an optional transition of 60 per cent, 70 per cent from 2029 and 80 per cent from 2032, and a compensation charge (6 euros per MWh at 60 to 80 per cent annual coverage) for shortfalls. Sites must also join automatic power-reduction schemes and can be disconnected to protect the system; water and PUE limits apply, and Article 5 sets data-location rules for high-category public systems. Minister Aagesen said that without the rule bills could rise by up to 5 billion euros. Caveat: operators contested feasibility; grid-queue effects are not yet visible. Country conversion: Spain now prices grid access for AI load in renewables and flexibility. [Signal 44, Confirmed, via BOE, 21 Nov 2026; MITECO, 20 Nov 2026; DCD, 23 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Apollo and Goldman price about $44 billion of notes to buy Vera Rubin GPUs for SpaceX

The deal was oversubscribed and upsized, with anchor commitments from BlackRock, Goldman Sachs Asset Management and KKR-advised accounts. Proceeds buy Nvidia Vera Rubin systems for SpaceX's terrestrial compute build; lease schedules start on delivery in the first half of 2027. IFR reports the public tranches price at 7.66 to 8.36 per cent, with the largest ($25.2 billion senior secured, due April 2033) at 8.259 per cent. Caveat: tranche detail is from IFR, not the press release. Country conversion: US compute is now financed as a leased asset class at high-yield coupons, and the collateral is next-generation Nvidia silicon. [Signal 48, Confirmed, via Apollo / Goldman Sachs press release, 20 Nov 2026; IFR; DCD, 23 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Trump threatens to block or tax US companies that build data centres abroad
item.description: At a White House press conference on 20 November, President Trump said: "We're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country," then added that if they do, "we're going to put a tremendous tax on them." He said he had not yet raised the idea with his staff and named China and Finland in his remarks. No rate, scope, start date or legal authority was given, and no presidential action or Federal Register rule had been published as of 21 November. Caveat: Congress holds the taxing power and the Supreme Court ruled in February 2026 that IEEPA does not authorise tariffs, so this is a stated intention, not policy. Country conversion: a credible penalty would tilt hyperscaler capex toward US sites and raise the political price of offshore campuses that host US-controlled silicon, at the same time as the BIS remote-access rule tightens Southeast Asia. [Signal 52, Corroborated, via CNBC, 20 Nov 2026; AP; Axios, 20 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire
